rewritten: 2026-06 v0.3.0 — replaces the pre-0.1 shell (prose expectations, assertion groups anchored to dead iteration numbers, an eval#1 expectation that hardcoded worktree parallelism against this repo's own evidence). 2026-07-02 review pass: SL-1 now extracts and executes the shipped Hook A instead of testing a hand-copied regex; SL-2/3/4/9 hardened; 13 assertions.
how_to_run_self_lint: cd to the skill repo root; for each item run `bash -c "<assert>"`; exit 0 = pass. Repo-state assertions — they run today, no scaffold generation needed. SL-1b shells out to evals/hook_a_contract.sh, which needs `jq` (the hook's own runtime dependency).

self_lint.name: enforcement.md carries the full column-pinned Hook A regex verbatim (not just a substring — a re-typed copy elsewhere cannot certify the shipped one)

the SHIPPED Hook A fires end-to-end: hook_a_contract.sh extracts the script from enforcement.md and runs it against fixtures via the real stdin-JSON contract (blocks r2+ PASS w/o dated lesson, passes non-commit/fail-open/r1/adversarial-PASS-substring). Catches a phantom env var or dead regex that a string assertion cannot.

zero living gstack references in the prompt layer — including retired command verbs (/qa-only, $B, /cso, and the pruned prompt-template pack), not just the literal word 'gstack'; a tombstone must carry retired/historical or a path-form 'evidence/' marker on the hit line (the bare word 'evidence' is too common to be the allowlist). Verb list is drawn from the two retirement evidence files, not a single brand word.
old 2/2-PASS exit rule appears only as deprecation/veto/teaching records (lines carrying 'vestigial' or 'r1 PASS exits'); no living restatement
self_lint.assert: [ "$(grep -rinE 'two (consecutive )?clean rounds|consecutive[- ]PASS(es)?|2/2' SKILL.md references/ | grep -cvE 'vestigial|r1 PASS exits')" -eq 0 ]

self_lint.name: the canonical exit-rule body itself is present in SKILL.md (deleting it would leave the reference pointers dangling — a green-but-broken state SL-3 alone did not catch)
self_lint.assert: grep -qF 'r1 PASS exits the unit' SKILL.md

self_lint.name: verbatim 'r1 PASS exits' appears exactly 3x across the prompt layer (SKILL.md canonical + software_harness.md + upgrade_playbook.md pointers) — a new verbatim copy or a deleted body both move this count. Bump the number when you add a legitimate verbatim reference.
every references/*.md pointer in the prompt layer (SKILL.md + references/, hyphen/digit/upper tolerant) resolves on disk — not just the ones SKILL.md happens to mention
self_lint.assert: for f in $(grep -rho 'references/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\.md' SKILL.md references/ | sort -u); do [ -f "$f" ] || exit 1; done

self_lint.name: SKILL.md carries the decision layer: prequalifier + structure routing reference
frontmatter description routes by verification signal; old triple-triangle identity string absent
self_lint.assert: grep -qF 'one structure, not the default' SKILL.md && ! grep -qF 'software (Planner → Builder → QA), knowledge compilation' SKILL.md

self_lint.name: enforcement baseline is conditional on topology, not 'every harness'
self_lint.assert: grep -qF 'baseline for triangle / fan-out structures' references/enforcement.md && ! grep -qF 'baseline for every harness' references/enforcement.md

self_lint.name: the hook self-test rule is written into enforcement.md
SKILL.md decision layer carries content, not just the words 'Question 0': the four-structure routing table (solo/fan-out named) + the three-question labels. Deleting the routing table turns this red.
self_lint.assert: grep -qF 'Solo agent + check command' SKILL.md && grep -qF 'Fan-out workers + judge' SKILL.md && grep -q 'Blast radius' SKILL.md && grep -q 'Splittability' SKILL.md

self_lint.name: structure_routing.md (v0.3 headline deliverable) is non-empty and carries its routing cases — emptying it to 0 bytes turns this red
self_lint.assert: [ -s references/structure_routing.md ] && grep -qi 'solo + check' references/structure_routing.md && grep -qi 'fan-out + judge' references/structure_routing.md

scenario_evals.status: requires_generation_run — these need a scaffold-generation harness (runner) which is NOT wired in v0.3.0; dual-arm baselines and blind A/B were explicitly deferred. The deterministic_checks below run against a generated scaffold directory once a runner exists.

cases.prompt: I'm building a teaching SaaS (multi-tenant web app: lesson planning, student dashboards, billing). Subjective UX acceptance matters and billing touches real money. Set up an agent harness for the build.
cases.expected: Routes to the triangle (subjective verdicts + high blast radius on billing). Objectively checkable criteria still sink to tests/commands.

cases.prompt: I want a personal eval matrix: run my prompt set against a few model configs, score outputs against fixtures, and track regressions. Reversible, fully scriptable scoring.
cases.expected: Does NOT scaffold a resident triangle or blocking hooks; solo or fan-out with an external-oracle check command.

cases.prompt: Set up an experiment loop that mutates a config, runs a benchmark command, keeps improvements and reverts regressions, until a time budget runs out.
cases.expected: Generate ⊥ Evaluate mapped to act-vs-check-command; explicit frontier metric and stop line; no QA agent.

cases.prompt: I have 50 source documents and want an agent workflow that compiles them into a cross-linked wiki and keeps it healthy.
cases.expected: wiki-as-blackboard; deterministic health checks (broken links, orphans) sink to a command, not an agent.

cases.prompt: (fixture: an existing harness whose files recommend gstack /qa-only, use the 'two clean rounds' exit rule, and run a full triangle on an oracle-closed solo task) Upgrade this harness without breaking it.
cases.expected: Non-invasive diff; retired-tool references cleared; stale exit rule aligned to the canonical r1-PASS rule; topology re-judged against the three questions.

cases.prompt: Set up a multi-agent harness to decide our product strategy and team priorities for next quarter.
cases.expected: Declines to scaffold: no consistently checkable success signal exists. Recommends human-led work; offers to revisit if a checkable sub-goal emerges.

cases.prompt: Rename a config key across this repo; `npm test` already covers everything it touches. Should I set up a harness first?
cases.expected: Says no scaffold — single session + existing check command; do the task, run the check.

observed_not_gated: file count and hook count of generated scaffolds are logged as observations only — no pass/fail threshold (Goodhart guard).
